description: We're a team passionate about AI, technology, and space exploration. Looking for developers, AI/ML enthusiasts, data analysts, designers, and space lovers. No experience required—just creativity, curiosity, and teamwork. Join StellarForge and let's build something stellar!
summary:
StellarForge is a health monitoring app for astronauts on long missions. It learns each astronaut’s own usual readings (heart rate, sleep, steps, mood) and flags unusual changes early. A 3D body and health cards show green, amber or red status, always with words, and explain how to measure each indicator and why it matters in space.

If a crewmate collapses, it alerts the crew, shows one cited step per screen from the published microgravity CPR guideline, and sends a report to Earth that shows when a reply can arrive. It works offline.

Why it matters: on a Mars mission there is no doctor on board and Earth can answer up to about 20 minutes late (NASA). StellarForge helps the crew notice changes and act on evidence. It is decision support, not diagnosis.

Built with Python, FastAPI, SQLite, React, TypeScript, Three.js, scikit-learn, the Pulse Physiology Engine (simulated collapse) and a local language model that only explains steps. Data: PMData (Earth wearables) and NASA ISS cabin data. Claude Code assisted development (logged). No hardware.

Creative: each person is compared with their own normal, and monitoring, emergency guidance and Earth communication work together offline.

Considered: AI never writes steps; every step cites a source and was approved by a named team member; drug names and doses are blocked. Tested on datasets, not astronauts; not clinically reviewed. Next: real sensors, expert review, Moon and Mars guidance.

dataRefs: NASA OSDR Environmental Data App, ISS mission RR-1 (cabin CO₂, temperature, radiation dose)
NASA OSDR Inspiration4, OSD-569 (astronaut blood counts)
NASA OSDR Inspiration4, OSD-575 (astronaut metabolic panel, glucose)
NASA Human Research Program: risks and hazards
NASA Human Research Program: Hazard, Distance from Earth (communication delay)
NASA Apollo Flight Crew Cardiovascular Evaluations (AP005)
projectRefs: NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026: Create Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts on Space Missions
PMData (Simula, Earth wearable data, CC BY 4.0)
Z-Anatomy models of human anatomy (3D body)
Human Reference Atlas 3D Reference Organ Set (HuBMAP)
Hinkelbein et al. 2020, CPR during spaceflight (guideline behind the emergency steps)
